title: Give a care manikin's ankle three passive range-of-motion repetitions, leg held on the bed, without forcing it
instruction: Work the ankle joint of the plastic training-manikin leg on the pad through its range three times, bending its foot up toward its shin and then pointing its toes down, gently and without forcing it and with the leg kept on the pad; finish with the foot back at rest and let go.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00, about 1.4 million US jobs) "exercise patients who are comatose, paralyzed, or have restricted mobility", to keep joints from stiffening. Ankle passive range of motion is Skill 15 of the national nurse aide exam (NNAAP): "While supporting the foot and ankle close to the bed, pushes/pulls foot toward head (dorsiflexion), and pushes/pulls foot down, toes point down (plantar flexion) (AT LEAST 3 TIMES...). Moves joints gently, slowly, and smoothly." Two hands are needed by the leg itself: it is loose and light, and pointing the toes takes more moment than the leg's weight holds down, so a hand on the foot alone levers the leg up and drags it; one hand holds the leg above the ankle while the other turns the foot.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Bed pad, fixed: firm foam in light blue vinyl, 24 x 64 x 1.2 cm, x 9.5 to 33.5, y -21.5 to 42.5; on it a foam leg trough: two walls 3 cm thick, 7 cm tall, 11.9 cm long (y 13.8 to 25.7), inner faces 5.53 cm either side of x 21.5, cradling the calf. (2) Training leg, loose: an adult woman's lower leg and foot at true size (ANSUR II women's means: foot 246 mm long, 93 mm wide; ankle 216 mm and calf 373 mm round; 438 mm floor to knee joint), hollow moulded vinyl-skinned shells, skin colour, friction 1.2; lower leg 0.30 kg (centre of mass 24 cm above the ankle), foot 0.15 kg. It lies on its back along +y, knee end toward the robot's left (y 33.2), on its heel and calf (tilted 7.2 deg, knee end up); the ankle axis (through the malleoli, 50 mm above the sole, 49 mm in front of the heel's back) at x 21.5, y -8.0, z 6.4, along x; toes up (top z 25.7). Black tape strips along the outer side of shin and foot. (3) The ankle: a hinge whose restoring moment stiffens toward each end: toward the shin 1.8 N m/rad to 10 deg, 5.4 to 20 deg, 18 beyond; toes down 1.2 to 20 deg, 3.0 to 45 deg, 15 beyond (0.79 N m at 15 deg up, 1.26 at 20 up, 0.94 at 30 down, 1.73 at 45 down); hard stops at 30 deg up, 55 deg down; at rest on its heel the foot sits 3 deg down. Build files and calibration: fabrication/ (STL, drawing). Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step: the ankle angle from neutral (up toward the shin positive), the heel's and the knee end's lowest points, where the knee end is, and each finger's collision-hull points. 0 for the rest of the run once a rule is broken: the foot pushed past the end of its range (more than 20 deg up or 45 deg down); the ankle jerked (angle changing faster than 90 deg/s between two control steps); the heel lifted more than 1 cm above where it lay; the knee end lifted more than 1 cm; the leg dragged more than 2 cm along the bed (knee end). Otherwise 0.25 per repetition, at most 0.75: a repetition is the foot up to 15 deg or more and down to 30 deg or more, one after the other (each counted only after the other has been reached since). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): three repetitions; at the end the foot within 5 deg of its resting angle, heel and knee end back down (within 5 mm of where they lay), every finger point 3 cm or more from leg and foot, leg and foot still (under 0.5 deg and 1 mm over 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: a phone films the leg's outer side with a protractor card and a ruler behind the ankle; angles, repetitions and speed come from the tape strips frame by frame (more than 3 deg between frames 1/30 s apart is a jerk), lifts from the ruler, drag from a tape mark on the pad beside the knee end.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the leg on its back in the trough with the heel on its taped mark on the pad and the knee end on its mark, foot upright and resting on the heel; check the ankle turns freely. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The leg is two rigid shells (smooth meshes from adult means, not a scan) on one hinge; it collides as their convex hulls, so the arch is filled. The ankle has no inversion, eversion or toe joints. Its passive moment is a piecewise-linear spring curve (set as the hinge's drive every step), lighter than a living ankle's, matched to the light training leg; the real leg reaches it with torsion springs and bump stops, checked by hanging weights. Skin and pad are rigid.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms reached in over the leg, the left above the lower leg and the right beside the foot, but neither took hold, the foot was not worked through its range and no repetition was made); demo: 1.0
